headline: Sensex plunges 1,000 points as US yields hit 2007 highs; Nifty falls below 22,300 amid global sell-off

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: US 10-year Treasury yields surged to 5.31%, the highest level since 2007
Rebound in global crude oil prices and concerns over global interest rate hikes
Indian benchmarks are set for their longest weekly losing run in 25 years
Global rate hikes sparking significant foreign fund outflows from benchmark shares
whatHappening: Sensex plunged 1,000 points, causing an investor wealth loss of ₹9.5 lakh crore within an hour
GST collections grew 14.7% to reach a record ₹2.03 lakh crore in September 2026
India's manufacturing PMI hit a seven-month high in September on strong demand
Auto and metal sectors emerged as the top draggers in today's market session
summary: Indian markets crashed as the Sensex dropped 1,000 points, tracking a surge in US 10-year yields to 5.31%. While domestic indicators like record GST collections and a strong manufacturing PMI showed resilience, global concerns triggered massive outflows. The benchmarks are currently witnessing their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years, with auto and metal stocks leading the decline.
